findings.claim: Review claim C-05: the task registry has NO lock and concurrent opens are last-write-wins.
findings.observed: docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md:514 heading '## The registry file itself has no lock', body at 516-519: '`.sbe/tasks.json` is rewritten atomically (write temp, rename), so it is never half-written, but two simultaneous `sbe task open` calls are last-write-wins and one of the two records can vanish... no service, no daemon, no lock.' This is REFUTED by the current code. src/brothersbe/tasks.py:225-289 defines `_registry_lock`, an `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` (line 270) taken on sidecar `.sbe/tasks.json.lock` (REGISTRY_LOCK_REL, line 91; opened at line 260), spun up to a 30s timeout (_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S, line 222) and raising RegistryUnusable rather than proceeding unlocked (lines 247-251, 277-281). `cmd_open` (line 406: `with _registry_lock(root):`) and `cmd_close` (line 501: `with _registry_lock(root):`) hold this lock across the ENTIRE read (load_registry) - decide - write (save_registry) critical section, added in commit db7296d ('Lock the stores that lost records...', Aug 1 2026). This is proven, not just claimed: tools/test_sbe_tasks.py:282-380 (class TestConcurrentWriters, test at line 360, `test_twenty_concurrent_writers_open_distinct_tasks_all_survive`) spawns 20 REAL separate subprocesses, each running the actual `sbe task open` CLI, released simultaneously from a filesystem barrier, and asserts all 20 survive as 20 distinct open tasks with none lost. I ran this suite myself: `python3 tools/test_sbe_tasks.py -v` -> 'Ran 18 tests in 10.559s / OK', with the concurrency test passing ('... ok'). git status before and after the run was unchanged (only pre-existing untracked files), so this verification had no side effects.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md:514-521. Replace the 'no lock' claim with: `sbe task open` and `sbe task close` now hold an exclusive `fcntl.flock` (tasks.py `_registry_lock`, lines 225-289) across the whole read-modify-write, so two concurrent `sbe task open`/`close` calls can no longer silently drop a record; proven by a 20-process test (tools/test_sbe_tasks.py:360). In the same edit, disclose the genuine residual gap this fix did NOT close: `sbe work remove` (src/brothersbe/work.py, cmd_remove, lines 557-601) still calls `load_registry`/`save_registry` directly at lines 559 and 601 without importing or holding `_registry_lock` at all (confirmed: work.py's imports at lines 28-48 never import `_registry_lock`), so a `sbe work remove --override-dirty` racing an `sbe task open`/`close` (or another `remove`) is still last-write-wins on that one path.

findings.claim: Same C-05 'no lock / last-write-wins' claim, repeated in the CLI reference doc.
findings.observed: docs/CLI.md:295-296: 'Concurrent writers of the registry file are out of scope (atomic rename, last write wins, no lock). Limits in full: `docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md`.' Contradicted by src/brothersbe/tasks.py:225-289/406/501 exactly as in the KNOWN-LIMITS.md finding above; this is the CLI reference page a developer reads to look up `sbe task` behavior, so it is the second-most load-bearing stale passage.
findings.recommended_fix: Update docs/CLI.md:295-296 to state that `open`/`close` serialize the read-modify-write under an exclusive flock (cite tasks.py `_registry_lock`), and that `sbe work remove` is the one entry point still outside that lock (src/brothersbe/work.py:559,601).

findings.claim: New finding, not in the original C-05 text: is the task registry lock complete across every writer, or does a residual unlocked path remain?
findings.observed: cmd_remove (work.py:557-617) calls `load_registry(root)` at line 559, and, when a dirty worktree needs an `--override-dirty` reason recorded, mutates `record["overrideDirty"]` and calls `save_registry(root, data)` at line 601 -- a read-modify-write on the SAME `.sbe/tasks.json` file `tasks.py` locks in `cmd_open`/`cmd_close`. work.py's imports (lines 28-48) never import `_registry_lock`, and grepping the whole function confirms no lock is acquired anywhere in it. Two concurrent callers (an `sbe work remove --override-dirty` racing another `remove`, or an `sbe task open`/`close`) can still race here exactly the way `cmd_open`/`cmd_close` used to before db7296d. This is not silently missed: CHANGELOG.md itself (around the db7296d entry, lines ~235-237) names this as 'a real residual race this change does not close', so the gap is honestly disclosed in the changelog even though none of the three docs flagged above (KNOWN-LIMITS.md, CLI.md, book/07) mention it.
findings.recommended_fix: Either wrap cmd_remove's read-modify-write in the same `_registry_lock(root)` context manager tasks.py already exports, or, if that is deliberately out of scope for this wave, say so explicitly in docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md next to the corrected lock description so the documentation names the ONE path that is still last-write-wins instead of implying (via silence) that the whole registry is now safe.
